title: The Logic Chain Breaking Point: A Controlled-Variable Benchmark for Reasoning Degradation in Open-Weight Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.20447v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We introduce The Logic Chain Breaking Point, a controlled-variable benchmark for deductive reasoning in open-weight language models. It spans three phases: (i) pure modus-ponens chain scaling, (ii) distractor resilience with a fixed core chain, and (iii) contradiction detection under primacy versus recency placement. Independent variables follow a powers-of-two sequence $v \in \{1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128\}$, with ground truth known by construction. We evaluate sixteen open-weight models across instruction-tuned and reasoning-tuned panels, including a small-model suite and a larger local-model extension. All models are evaluated with greedy decoding under model-appropriate context and output budgets, while context- and length-limited trials are quarantined from the valid accuracy denominator. tldr: 该论文提出了“逻辑链断裂点”基准，通过控制变量的方法系统评估开放权重语言模型在多步演绎推理链扩展、干扰项抗性和矛盾检测中的推理退化现象，发现难度呈现急剧的非单调变化。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "The Logic Chain Breaking Point," a controlled-variable benchmark that systematically evaluates reasoning degradation in open-weight language models across modus-ponens chain scaling, distractor resilience, and contradiction detection, revealing a sharply non-monotonic difficulty surface.
